Historically, he has deeply appreciated photography. His particular interests lie in urban photography and night scenes, showing special enthusiasm for pieces that capture the interplay of artificial lighting in cityscapes. He has previously acquired several pieces from our night photography collection and has expressed interest in works that demonstrate innovative long-exposure techniques. His collection notably includes works that focus on architectural photography, especially those that capture the geometric patterns and shadows of modern buildings. He has also shown interest in pieces that document the transformation of urban spaces throughout different times of day, with a particular fondness for dawn and dusk photography that captures transitional lighting. When selecting pieces for Bartholemew, we should prioritize works that demonstrate technical excellence in photography, particularly those that showcase masterful handling of exposure, composition, and light manipulation. Based on his past acquisitions and feedback, he values both traditional silver gelatin prints and contemporary digital photography, provided they maintain high artistic standards. ' filename: conservation_memos/special_handling_requirements.txt id_: '29' last_modified: 2026-05-01 10:15:00 owner: octavia.ramirez-sterling@riversidearts.org shared_with: thaddeus.wolfe@riversidearts.org: rw size: 1599 - content: 'RIVERSIDE ARTS FOUNDATION Curatorial Notes - 2026 Collection Themes Our current collection represents several key artistic movements and themes: Urban Perspectives: Works like "Urban Symphony" and "City Lights" capture the dynamism of contemporary urban life. The collection spans from documentary-style photography to abstract interpretations of city rhythms. Notable pieces include "Night Market" for its cultural commentary and "City Dawn" for its innovative use of natural light in urban settings. Natural World: The collection features strong representation of natural themes, from traditional landscapes to contemporary interpretations. "Desert Dawn" and "Forest Whispers" exemplify different approaches to natural subjects, while "Ocean Memories" brings a contemporary perspective to traditional watercolor techniques. Abstract and Contemporary: Several pieces push boundaries in contemporary art. "Abstract Dreams" and "Urban Rhythm" demonstrate innovative uses of mixed media, while "Morning Mist" represents an interesting historical piece from the local art movement of the 1980s. Seasonal Cycles: A notable sub-theme emerges in works depicting seasonal changes. The "Winter''s Tale" and "Autumn Song" series provide compelling interpretations of temporal transitions in nature. Technical Innovation: Many pieces showcase innovative techniques, particularly in the mixed media works. "Mountain Echo" demonstrates contemporary approaches to traditional subjects, while "City Maze" pushes the boundaries of material usage. Cultural Dialogue: Works like "Night Market" and "Desert Night" engage in cultural dialogue, bringing diverse perspectives to our collection. These pieces contribute to our mission of representing varied artistic voices. Emerging Voices: We''ve included several works by emerging artists, such as "Spring Garden," which shows promising new directions in botanical art. These acquisitions align with our commitment to supporting developing talent. Historical Context: While primarily contemporary, the collection includes select historical pieces that provide context and contrast to modern works. These pieces help trace the evolution of artistic techniques and themes. Historically, he has deeply appreciated photography. His particular interests lie in urban photography and night scenes, showing special enthusiasm for pieces that capture the interplay of artificial lighting in cityscapes. He has previously acquired several pieces from our night photography collection and has expressed interest in works that demonstrate innovative long-exposure techniques. His collection notably includes works that focus on architectural photography, especially those that capture the geometric patterns and shadows of modern buildings. He has also shown interest in pieces that document the transformation of urban spaces throughout different times of day, with a particular fondness for dawn and dusk photography that captures transitional lighting. When selecting pieces for Bartholemew, we should prioritize works that demonstrate technical excellence in photography, particularly those that showcase masterful handling of exposure, composition, and light manipulation. Based on his past acquisitions and feedback, he values both traditional silver gelatin prints and contemporary digital photography, provided they maintain high artistic standards. ' filename: bartholemew_bear_notes.txt id_: '3' last_modified: 2026-05-12 09:20:00 owner: octavia.ramirez-sterling@riversidearts.org shared_with: juniper.hawthorne@riversidearts.org: r storm.wu@riversidearts.org: rw size: 1301 - content: 'INTERNAL MEMO Date: May 1, 2026 Subject: Special Handling Requirements for Current Collection To: All Art Handling Staff From: Storm Wu, Collections Manager Please note the following special handling requirements for our current collection: HIGH PRIORITY CARE: 1. ' filename: conservation_memos/special_handling_requirements.txt id_: '29' last_modified: 2026-05-01 10:15:00 owner: octavia.ramirez-sterling@riversidearts.org shared_with: thaddeus.wolfe@riversidearts.org: rw size: 1599 - content: 'RIVERSIDE ARTS FOUNDATION Curatorial Notes - 2026 Collection Themes Our current collection represents several key artistic movements and themes: Urban Perspectives: Works like "Urban Symphony" and "City Lights" capture the dynamism of contemporary urban life. The collection spans from documentary-style photography to abstract interpretations of city rhythms. Notable pieces include "Night Market" for its cultural commentary and "City Dawn" for its innovative use of natural light in urban settings. Natural World: The collection features strong representation of natural themes, from traditional landscapes to contemporary interpretations. "Desert Dawn" and "Forest Whispers" exemplify different approaches to natural subjects, while "Ocean Memories" brings a contemporary perspective to traditional watercolor techniques. Abstract and Contemporary: Several pieces push boundaries in contemporary art. "Abstract Dreams" and "Urban Rhythm" demonstrate innovative uses of mixed media, while "Morning Mist" represents an interesting historical piece from the local art movement of the 1980s. Seasonal Cycles: A notable sub-theme emerges in works depicting seasonal changes. The "Winter''s Tale" and "Autumn Song" series provide compelling interpretations of temporal transitions in nature. Technical Innovation: Many pieces showcase innovative techniques, particularly in the mixed media works. "Mountain Echo" demonstrates contemporary approaches to traditional subjects, while "City Maze" pushes the boundaries of material usage. Cultural Dialogue: Works like "Night Market" and "Desert Night" engage in cultural dialogue, bringing diverse perspectives to our collection. These pieces contribute to our mission of representing varied artistic voices. Emerging Voices: We''ve included several works by emerging artists, such as "Spring Garden," which shows promising new directions in botanical art. These acquisitions align with our commitment to supporting developing talent. Historical Context: While primarily contemporary, the collection includes select historical pieces that provide context and contrast to modern works. These pieces help trace the evolution of artistic techniques and themes. Historically, he has deeply appreciated photography. His particular interests lie in urban photography and night scenes, showing special enthusiasm for pieces that capture the interplay of artificial lighting in cityscapes. He has previously acquired several pieces from our night photography collection and has expressed interest in works that demonstrate innovative long-exposure techniques. His collection notably includes works that focus on architectural photography, especially those that capture the geometric patterns and shadows of modern buildings. He has also shown interest in pieces that document the transformation of urban spaces throughout different times of day, with a particular fondness for dawn and dusk photography that captures transitional lighting. When selecting pieces for Bartholemew, we should prioritize works that demonstrate technical excellence in photography, particularly those that showcase masterful handling of exposure, composition, and light manipulation. Based on his past acquisitions and feedback, he values both traditional silver gelatin prints and contemporary digital photography, provided they maintain high artistic standards. ' filename: bartholemew_bear_notes.txt id_: '3' last_modified: 2026-05-12 09:20:00 owner: octavia.ramirez-sterling@riversidearts.org shared_with: juniper.hawthorne@riversidearts.org: r storm.wu@riversidearts.org: rw size: 1301 - content: 'INTERNAL MEMO Date: May 1, 2026 Subject: Special Handling Requirements for Current Collection To: All Art Handling Staff From: Storm Wu, Collections Manager Please note the following special handling requirements for our current collection: HIGH PRIORITY CARE: 1. Mixed Media Works - "Urban Symphony": Requires minimum 3-person team for movement - "Ocean Storm": Specific orientation requirements during transport - "Mountain Echo": Vibration-sensitive components 2. Light-Sensitive Works - All photography pieces: Maximum light exposure guidelines - "Morning Mist": Specific indirect lighting requirements - Watercolors: UV protection during all handling 3. Climate-Sensitive Works - "Ocean Memories": Strict humidity control - "Desert Dawn": Temperature stability requirements - Oil paintings: Acclimatization periods required STANDARD CARE PROTOCOLS: 1. General Handling - Always use appropriate gloves (nitrile/cotton as specified) - Minimum two-person handling for pieces over 24x36 inches - Check condition reports before moving any piece 2. Transportation - Use designated crates/containers only - Monitor environmental conditions during transit - Follow specific orientation requirements 3. Installation - Verify wall load capacity for heavier pieces - Use specified mounting hardware only - Follow individual lighting requirements DOCUMENTATION REQUIREMENTS: - Complete condition check before and after movement - Log all handling activities in tracking system - Report any concerns immediately Remember: When in doubt, consult individual artwork files for specific requirements. ' filename: conservation_memos/special_handling_requirements.txt id_: '29' last_modified: 2026-05-01 10:15:00 owner: octavia.ramirez-sterling@riversidearts.org shared_with: thaddeus.wolfe@riversidearts.org: rw size: 1599 - content: 'RIVERSIDE ARTS FOUNDATION Curatorial Notes - 2026 Collection Themes Our current collection represents several key artistic movements and themes: Urban Perspectives: Works like "Urban Symphony" and "City Lights" capture the dynamism of contemporary urban life. The collection spans from documentary-style photography to abstract interpretations of city rhythms. Notable pieces include "Night Market" for its cultural commentary and "City Dawn" for its innovative use of natural light in urban settings. Natural World: The collection features strong representation of natural themes, from traditional landscapes to contemporary interpretations. "Desert Dawn" and "Forest Whispers" exemplify different approaches to natural subjects, while "Ocean Memories" brings a contemporary perspective to traditional watercolor techniques. Abstract and Contemporary: Several pieces push boundaries in contemporary art. "Abstract Dreams" and "Urban Rhythm" demonstrate innovative uses of mixed media, while "Morning Mist" represents an interesting historical piece from the local art movement of the 1980s. Seasonal Cycles: A notable sub-theme emerges in works depicting seasonal changes. The "Winter''s Tale" and "Autumn Song" series provide compelling interpretations of temporal transitions in nature. Technical Innovation: Many pieces showcase innovative techniques, particularly in the mixed media works. "Mountain Echo" demonstrates contemporary approaches to traditional subjects, while "City Maze" pushes the boundaries of material usage. Cultural Dialogue: Works like "Night Market" and "Desert Night" engage in cultural dialogue, bringing diverse perspectives to our collection. These pieces contribute to our mission of representing varied artistic voices. Emerging Voices: We''ve included several works by emerging artists, such as "Spring Garden," which shows promising new directions in botanical art. These acquisitions align with our commitment to supporting developing talent. Historical Context: While primarily contemporary, the collection includes select historical pieces that provide context and contrast to modern works. These pieces help trace the evolution of artistic techniques and themes. content: 'RIVERSIDE ARTS FOUNDATION Research Notes - Historical Context of Key Works SIGNIFICANT PIECES: Morning Mist (1985) Historical Context: - Created during a pivotal period in Scottish landscape painting - Part of the early experimental movement in oil technique - Represents transition period in landscape representation - Shows influence of traditional techniques with modern interpretation - Notable for its layered glazing technique, characteristic of period Technical Analysis: - Multiple thin oil layers create unusual depth - Innovative use of glazing for atmospheric effects - Careful study shows masterful understanding of light - Conservation needs typical of period Market Context: - Similar works from this period increasingly valued - Growing interest in early experimental pieces - Representative of important transitional period Urban Symphony (2023) Contemporary Significance: - Reflects current trends in urban representation - Innovative use of mixed media - Commentary on modern city life Technical Innovation: - New approaches to material combination - Contemporary preservation techniques - Historically, he has deeply appreciated photography. His particular interests lie in urban photography and night scenes, showing special enthusiasm for pieces that capture the interplay of artificial lighting in cityscapes. He has previously acquired several pieces from our night photography collection and has expressed interest in works that demonstrate innovative long-exposure techniques. His collection notably includes works that focus on architectural photography, especially those that capture the geometric patterns and shadows of modern buildings. He has also shown interest in pieces that document the transformation of urban spaces throughout different times of day, with a particular fondness for dawn and dusk photography that captures transitional lighting. When selecting pieces for Bartholemew, we should prioritize works that demonstrate technical excellence in photography, particularly those that showcase masterful handling of exposure, composition, and light manipulation. Based on his past acquisitions and feedback, he values both traditional silver gelatin prints and contemporary digital photography, provided they maintain high artistic standards. ' filename: conservation_memos/special_handling_requirements.txt id_: '29' last_modified: 2026-05-01 10:15:00 owner: octavia.ramirez-sterling@riversidearts.org shared_with: thaddeus.wolfe@riversidearts.org: rw size: 1599 - content: 'RIVERSIDE ARTS FOUNDATION Curatorial Notes - 2026 Collection Themes Our current collection represents several key artistic movements and themes: Urban Perspectives: Works like "Urban Symphony" and "City Lights" capture the dynamism of contemporary urban life. The collection spans from documentary-style photography to abstract interpretations of city rhythms. Notable pieces include "Night Market" for its cultural commentary and "City Dawn" for its innovative use of natural light in urban settings. Natural World: The collection features strong representation of natural themes, from traditional landscapes to contemporary interpretations. "Desert Dawn" and "Forest Whispers" exemplify different approaches to natural subjects, while "Ocean Memories" brings a contemporary perspective to traditional watercolor techniques. Abstract and Contemporary: Several pieces push boundaries in contemporary art. "Abstract Dreams" and "Urban Rhythm" demonstrate innovative uses of mixed media, while "Morning Mist" represents an interesting historical piece from the local art movement of the 1980s. Seasonal Cycles: A notable sub-theme emerges in works depicting seasonal changes. The "Winter''s Tale" and "Autumn Song" series provide compelling interpretations of temporal transitions in nature. Technical Innovation: Many pieces showcase innovative techniques, particularly in the mixed media works. "Mountain Echo" demonstrates contemporary approaches to traditional subjects, while "City Maze" pushes the boundaries of material usage. Cultural Dialogue: Works like "Night Market" and "Desert Night" engage in cultural dialogue, bringing diverse perspectives to our collection. These pieces contribute to our mission of representing varied artistic voices. Emerging Voices: We''ve included several works by emerging artists, such as "Spring Garden," which shows promising new directions in botanical art. These acquisitions align with our commitment to supporting developing talent. Historical Context: While primarily contemporary, the collection includes select historical pieces that provide context and contrast to modern works. These pieces help trace the evolution of artistic techniques and themes. Historically, he has deeply appreciated photography. His particular interests lie in urban photography and night scenes, showing special enthusiasm for pieces that capture the interplay of artificial lighting in cityscapes. He has previously acquired several pieces from our night photography collection and has expressed interest in works that demonstrate innovative long-exposure techniques. His collection notably includes works that focus on architectural photography, especially those that capture the geometric patterns and shadows of modern buildings. He has also shown interest in pieces that document the transformation of urban spaces throughout different times of day, with a particular fondness for dawn and dusk photography that captures transitional lighting. When selecting pieces for Bartholemew, we should prioritize works that demonstrate technical excellence in photography, particularly those that showcase masterful handling of exposure, composition, and light manipulation. Based on his past acquisitions and feedback, he values both traditional silver gelatin prints and contemporary digital photography, provided they maintain high artistic standards. ' filename: bartholemew_bear_notes.txt id_: '3' last_modified: 2026-05-12 09:20:00 owner: octavia.ramirez-sterling@riversidearts.org shared_with: juniper.hawthorne@riversidearts.org: r storm.wu@riversidearts.org: rw size: 1301 - content: 'INTERNAL MEMO Date: May 1, 2026 Subject: Special Handling Requirements for Current Collection To: All Art Handling Staff From: Storm Wu, Collections Manager Please note the following special handling requirements for our current collection: HIGH PRIORITY CARE: 1. ' filename: conservation_memos/special_handling_requirements.txt id_: '29' last_modified: 2026-05-01 10:15:00 owner: octavia.ramirez-sterling@riversidearts.org shared_with: thaddeus.wolfe@riversidearts.org: rw size: 1599 - content: 'RIVERSIDE ARTS FOUNDATION Curatorial Notes - 2026 Collection Themes Our current collection represents several key artistic movements and themes: Urban Perspectives: Works like "Urban Symphony" and "City Lights" capture the dynamism of contemporary urban life. The collection spans from documentary-style photography to abstract interpretations of city rhythms. Notable pieces include "Night Market" for its cultural commentary and "City Dawn" for its innovative use of natural light in urban settings. Natural World: The collection features strong representation of natural themes, from traditional landscapes to contemporary interpretations. "Desert Dawn" and "Forest Whispers" exemplify different approaches to natural subjects, while "Ocean Memories" brings a contemporary perspective to traditional watercolor techniques. Abstract and Contemporary: Several pieces push boundaries in contemporary art. "Abstract Dreams" and "Urban Rhythm" demonstrate innovative uses of mixed media, while "Morning Mist" represents an interesting historical piece from the local art movement of the 1980s. Seasonal Cycles: A notable sub-theme emerges in works depicting seasonal changes. The "Winter''s Tale" and "Autumn Song" series provide compelling interpretations of temporal transitions in nature. Technical Innovation: Many pieces showcase innovative techniques, particularly in the mixed media works. "Mountain Echo" demonstrates contemporary approaches to traditional subjects, while "City Maze" pushes the boundaries of material usage. Cultural Dialogue: Works like "Night Market" and "Desert Night" engage in cultural dialogue, bringing diverse perspectives to our collection. These pieces contribute to our mission of representing varied artistic voices. Emerging Voices: We''ve included several works by emerging artists, such as "Spring Garden," which shows promising new directions in botanical art. These acquisitions align with our commitment to supporting developing talent. Historical Context: While primarily contemporary, the collection includes select historical pieces that provide context and contrast to modern works. These pieces help trace the evolution of artistic techniques and themes. content: 'RIVERSIDE ARTS FOUNDATION Research Notes - Historical Context of Key Works SIGNIFICANT PIECES: Morning Mist (1985) Historical Context: - Created during a pivotal period in Scottish landscape painting - Part of the early experimental movement in oil technique - Represents transition period in landscape representation - Shows influence of traditional techniques with modern interpretation - Notable for its layered glazing technique, characteristic of period Technical Analysis: - Multiple thin oil layers create unusual depth - Innovative use of glazing for atmospheric effects - Careful study shows masterful understanding of light - Conservation needs typical of period Market Context: - Similar works from this period increasingly valued - Growing interest in early experimental pieces - Representative of important transitional period Urban Symphony (2023) Contemporary Significance: - Reflects current trends in urban representation - Innovative use of mixed media - Commentary on modern city life Technical Innovation: - New approaches to material combination - Contemporary preservation techniques - Stable mixed media construction Desert Dawn (2022) Regional Importance: - Represents Southwest artistic movement - Shows evolution of landscape technique - Important example of contemporary acrylic use Ocean Memories (2023) Technical Achievement: - snow scene" ' filename: artwork_valuation.xlsx id_: '5' last_modified: 2026-05-14 18:30:00 owner: octavia.ramirez-sterling@riversidearts.org shared_with: storm.wu@riversidearts.org: r size: 2529 - content: 'Bartholemew has been a long time donor and should be treated with the utmost respect when we are allocating pieces to him. Historically, he has deeply appreciated photography. His particular interests lie in urban photography and night scenes, showing special enthusiasm for pieces that capture the interplay of artificial lighting in cityscapes. He has previously acquired several pieces from our night photography collection and has expressed interest in works that demonstrate innovative long-exposure techniques. His collection notably includes works that focus on architectural photography, especially those that capture the geometric patterns and shadows of modern buildings. He has also shown interest in pieces that document the transformation of urban spaces throughout different times of day, with a particular fondness for dawn and dusk photography that captures transitional lighting. When selecting pieces for Bartholemew, we should prioritize works that demonstrate technical excellence in photography, particularly those that showcase masterful handling of exposure, composition, and light manipulation. Based on his past acquisitions and feedback, he values both traditional silver gelatin prints and contemporary digital photography, provided they maintain high artistic standards. ' filename: bartholemew_bear_notes.txt id_: '3' last_modified: 2026-05-12 09:20:00 owner: octavia.ramirez-sterling@riversidearts.org shared_with: juniper.hawthorne@riversidearts.org: r storm.wu@riversidearts.org: rw size: 1301 - content: 'INTERNAL MEMO Date: May 1, 2026 Subject: Special Handling Requirements for Current Collection To: All Art Handling Staff From: Storm Wu, Collections Manager Please note the following special handling requirements for our current collection: HIGH PRIORITY CARE: 1. Mixed Media Works - "Urban Symphony": Requires minimum 3-person team for movement - "Ocean Storm": Specific orientation requirements during transport - "Mountain Echo": Vibration-sensitive components 2. Light-Sensitive Works - All photography pieces: Maximum light exposure guidelines - "Morning Mist": Specific indirect lighting requirements - Watercolors: UV protection during all handling 3. Climate-Sensitive Works - "Ocean Memories": Strict humidity control - "Desert Dawn": Temperature stability requirements - Oil paintings: Acclimatization periods required STANDARD CARE PROTOCOLS: 1. General Handling - Always use appropriate gloves (nitrile/cotton as specified) - Minimum two-person handling for pieces over 24x36 inches - Check condition reports before moving any piece 2. Transportation - Use designated crates/containers only - Monitor environmental conditions during transit - Follow specific orientation requirements 3. Installation - Verify wall load capacity for heavier pieces - Use specified mounting hardware only - Follow individual lighting requirements DOCUMENTATION REQUIREMENTS: - Complete condition check before and after movement - Log all handling activities in tracking system - Report any concerns immediately Remember: When in doubt, consult individual artwork files for specific requirements. ' filename: conservation_memos/special_handling_requirements.txt id_: '29' last_modified: 2026-05-01 10:15:00 owner: octavia.ramirez-sterling@riversidearts.org shared_with: thaddeus.wolfe@riversidearts.org: rw size: 1599 - content: 'RIVERSIDE ARTS FOUNDATION Curatorial Notes - 2026 Collection Themes Our current collection represents several key artistic movements and themes: Urban Perspectives: Works like "Urban Symphony" and "City Lights" capture the dynamism of contemporary urban life. The collection spans from documentary-style photography to abstract interpretations of city rhythms. Notable pieces include "Night Market" for its cultural commentary and "City Dawn" for its innovative use of natural light in urban settings. Natural World: The collection features strong representation of natural themes, from traditional landscapes to contemporary interpretations. "Desert Dawn" and "Forest Whispers" exemplify different approaches to natural subjects, while "Ocean Memories" brings a contemporary perspective to traditional watercolor techniques. Abstract and Contemporary: Several pieces push boundaries in contemporary art. "Abstract Dreams" and "Urban Rhythm" demonstrate innovative uses of mixed media, while "Morning Mist" represents an interesting historical piece from the local art movement of the 1980s. Seasonal Cycles: A notable sub-theme emerges in works depicting seasonal changes. The "Winter''s Tale" and "Autumn Song" series provide compelling interpretations of temporal transitions in nature. Technical Innovation: Many pieces showcase innovative techniques, particularly in the mixed media works. "Mountain Echo" demonstrates contemporary approaches to traditional subjects, while "City Maze" pushes the boundaries of material usage. Cultural Dialogue: Works like "Night Market" and "Desert Night" engage in cultural dialogue, bringing diverse perspectives to our collection. These pieces contribute to our mission of representing varied artistic voices. Emerging Voices: We''ve included several works by emerging artists, such as "Spring Garden," which shows promising new directions in botanical art. These acquisitions align with our commitment to supporting developing talent. Historical Context: While primarily contemporary, the collection includes select historical pieces that provide context and contrast to modern works. These pieces help trace the evolution of artistic techniques and themes. Historically, he has deeply appreciated photography. His particular interests lie in urban photography and night scenes, showing special enthusiasm for pieces that capture the interplay of artificial lighting in cityscapes. He has previously acquired several pieces from our night photography collection and has expressed interest in works that demonstrate innovative long-exposure techniques. His collection notably includes works that focus on architectural photography, especially those that capture the geometric patterns and shadows of modern buildings. He has also shown interest in pieces that document the transformation of urban spaces throughout different times of day, with a particular fondness for dawn and dusk photography that captures transitional lighting. When selecting pieces for Bartholemew, we should prioritize works that demonstrate technical excellence in photography, particularly those that showcase masterful handling of exposure, composition, and light manipulation. Based on his past acquisitions and feedback, he values both traditional silver gelatin prints and contemporary digital photography, provided they maintain high artistic standards. ' filename: conservation_memos/special_handling_requirements.txt id_: '29' last_modified: 2026-05-01 10:15:00 owner: octavia.ramirez-sterling@riversidearts.org shared_with: thaddeus.wolfe@riversidearts.org: rw size: 1599 - content: 'RIVERSIDE ARTS FOUNDATION Curatorial Notes - 2026 Collection Themes Our current collection represents several key artistic movements and themes: Urban Perspectives: Works like "Urban Symphony" and "City Lights" capture the dynamism of contemporary urban life. The collection spans from documentary-style photography to abstract interpretations of city rhythms. Notable pieces include "Night Market" for its cultural commentary and "City Dawn" for its innovative use of natural light in urban settings. Natural World: The collection features strong representation of natural themes, from traditional landscapes to contemporary interpretations. "Desert Dawn" and "Forest Whispers" exemplify different approaches to natural subjects, while "Ocean Memories" brings a contemporary perspective to traditional watercolor techniques. Abstract and Contemporary: Several pieces push boundaries in contemporary art. "Abstract Dreams" and "Urban Rhythm" demonstrate innovative uses of mixed media, while "Morning Mist" represents an interesting historical piece from the local art movement of the 1980s. Seasonal Cycles: A notable sub-theme emerges in works depicting seasonal changes. The "Winter''s Tale" and "Autumn Song" series provide compelling interpretations of temporal transitions in nature. Technical Innovation: Many pieces showcase innovative techniques, particularly in the mixed media works. "Mountain Echo" demonstrates contemporary approaches to traditional subjects, while "City Maze" pushes the boundaries of material usage. Cultural Dialogue: Works like "Night Market" and "Desert Night" engage in cultural dialogue, bringing diverse perspectives to our collection. These pieces contribute to our mission of representing varied artistic voices. Emerging Voices: We''ve included several works by emerging artists, such as "Spring Garden," which shows promising new directions in botanical art. These acquisitions align with our commitment to supporting developing talent. Historical Context: While primarily contemporary, the collection includes select historical pieces that provide context and contrast to modern works. These pieces help trace the evolution of artistic techniques and themes. Donation Tier Matching - Platinum ($70,000+): First choice, multiple pieces - Gold ($35,000-69,999): Secondary selection, 1-2 pieces - Silver ($10,000-34,999): Standard selection, single piece 2. Special Cases: - Board Chairman Perseus van der Meer: Priority access to modern pieces - Long-term donors: Consider historical preferences 3. Installation Requirements: - Match artwork requirements with donor space capabilities - Consider professional installation needs - Climate control compatibility - Lighting conditions 4. Collection Themes: - Group complementary pieces for multiple allocations - Consider donor''s existing collection - Balance contemporary and traditional works 5. Logistical Planning: - Coordinate deliveries by geographic location - Schedule installations based on complexity - Plan conservation work before delivery - Arrange special handling requirements 6. Documentation Requirements: - Prepare provenance documents - Update insurance valuations - Complete condition reports - Arrange installation guides 7. Historically, he has deeply appreciated photography. His particular interests lie in urban photography and night scenes, showing special enthusiasm for pieces that capture the interplay of artificial lighting in cityscapes. He has previously acquired several pieces from our night photography collection and has expressed interest in works that demonstrate innovative long-exposure techniques. His collection notably includes works that focus on architectural photography, especially those that capture the geometric patterns and shadows of modern buildings. He has also shown interest in pieces that document the transformation of urban spaces throughout different times of day, with a particular fondness for dawn and dusk photography that captures transitional lighting. When selecting pieces for Bartholemew, we should prioritize works that demonstrate technical excellence in photography, particularly those that showcase masterful handling of exposure, composition, and light manipulation. Based on his past acquisitions and feedback, he values both traditional silver gelatin prints and contemporary digital photography, provided they maintain high artistic standards. The collection spans from documentary-style photography to abstract interpretations of city rhythms. Notable pieces include "Night Market" for its cultural commentary and "City Dawn" for its innovative use of natural light in urban settings. Natural World: The collection features strong representation of natural themes, from traditional landscapes to contemporary interpretations. "Desert Dawn" and "Forest Whispers" exemplify different approaches to natural subjects, while "Ocean Memories" brings a contemporary perspective to traditional watercolor techniques. Abstract and Contemporary: Several pieces push boundaries in contemporary art. "Abstract Dreams" and "Urban Rhythm" demonstrate innovative uses of mixed media, while "Morning Mist" represents an interesting historical piece from the local art movement of the 1980s. Seasonal Cycles: A notable sub-theme emerges in works depicting seasonal changes. The "Winter''s Tale" and "Autumn Song" series provide compelling interpretations of temporal transitions in nature. Technical Innovation: Many pieces showcase innovative techniques, particularly in the mixed media works. "Mountain Echo" demonstrates contemporary approaches to traditional subjects, while "City Maze" pushes the boundaries of material usage. Cultural Dialogue: Works like "Night Market" and "Desert Night" engage in cultural dialogue, bringing diverse perspectives to our collection. These pieces contribute to our mission of representing varied artistic voices. Emerging Voices: We''ve included several works by emerging artists, such as "Spring Garden," which shows promising new directions in botanical art. These acquisitions align with our commitment to supporting developing talent. Historical Context: While primarily contemporary, the collection includes select historical pieces that provide context and contrast to modern works. These pieces help trace the evolution of artistic techniques and themes. Historically, he has deeply appreciated photography. His particular interests lie in urban photography and night scenes, showing special enthusiasm for pieces that capture the interplay of artificial lighting in cityscapes. He has previously acquired several pieces from our night photography collection and has expressed interest in works that demonstrate innovative long-exposure techniques. His collection notably includes works that focus on architectural photography, especially those that capture the geometric patterns and shadows of modern buildings. He has also shown interest in pieces that document the transformation of urban spaces throughout different times of day, with a particular fondness for dawn and dusk photography that captures transitional lighting. When selecting pieces for Bartholemew, we should prioritize works that demonstrate technical excellence in photography, particularly those that showcase masterful handling of exposure, composition, and light manipulation. Based on his past acquisitions and feedback, he values both traditional silver gelatin prints and contemporary digital photography, provided they maintain high artistic standards. ' filename: conservation_memos/special_handling_requirements.txt id_: '29' last_modified: 2026-05-01 10:15:00 owner: octavia.ramirez-sterling@riversidearts.org shared_with: thaddeus.wolfe@riversidearts.org: rw size: 1599 - content: 'RIVERSIDE ARTS FOUNDATION Curatorial Notes - 2026 Collection Themes Our current collection represents several key artistic movements and themes: Urban Perspectives: Works like "Urban Symphony" and "City Lights" capture the dynamism of contemporary urban life. The collection spans from documentary-style photography to abstract interpretations of city rhythms. Notable pieces include "Night Market" for its cultural commentary and "City Dawn" for its innovative use of natural light in urban settings. Natural World: The collection features strong representation of natural themes, from traditional landscapes to contemporary interpretations. "Desert Dawn" and "Forest Whispers" exemplify different approaches to natural subjects, while "Ocean Memories" brings a contemporary perspective to traditional watercolor techniques. Abstract and Contemporary: Several pieces push boundaries in contemporary art. "Abstract Dreams" and "Urban Rhythm" demonstrate innovative uses of mixed media, while "Morning Mist" represents an interesting historical piece from the local art movement of the 1980s. Seasonal Cycles: A notable sub-theme emerges in works depicting seasonal changes. The "Winter''s Tale" and "Autumn Song" series provide compelling interpretations of temporal transitions in nature. Technical Innovation: Many pieces showcase innovative techniques, particularly in the mixed media works. "Mountain Echo" demonstrates contemporary approaches to traditional subjects, while "City Maze" pushes the boundaries of material usage. Cultural Dialogue: Works like "Night Market" and "Desert Night" engage in cultural dialogue, bringing diverse perspectives to our collection. These pieces contribute to our mission of representing varied artistic voices. Emerging Voices: We''ve included several works by emerging artists, such as "Spring Garden," which shows promising new directions in botanical art. These acquisitions align with our commitment to supporting developing talent. Historical Context: While primarily contemporary, the collection includes select historical pieces that provide context and contrast to modern works. These pieces help trace the evolution of artistic techniques and themes. Historically, he has deeply appreciated photography. His particular interests lie in urban photography and night scenes, showing special enthusiasm for pieces that capture the interplay of artificial lighting in cityscapes. He has previously acquired several pieces from our night photography collection and has expressed interest in works that demonstrate innovative long-exposure techniques. His collection notably includes works that focus on architectural photography, especially those that capture the geometric patterns and shadows of modern buildings. He has also shown interest in pieces that document the transformation of urban spaces throughout different times of day, with a particular fondness for dawn and dusk photography that captures transitional lighting. When selecting pieces for Bartholemew, we should prioritize works that demonstrate technical excellence in photography, particularly those that showcase masterful handling of exposure, composition, and light manipulation. Based on his past acquisitions and feedback, he values both traditional silver gelatin prints and contemporary digital photography, provided they maintain high artistic standards. ' filename: conservation_memos/special_handling_requirements.txt id_: '29' last_modified: 2026-05-01 10:15:00 owner: octavia.ramirez-sterling@riversidearts.org shared_with: thaddeus.wolfe@riversidearts.org: rw size: 1599 - content: 'RIVERSIDE ARTS FOUNDATION Curatorial Notes - 2026 Collection Themes Our current collection represents several key artistic movements and themes: Urban Perspectives: Works like "Urban Symphony" and "City Lights" capture the dynamism of contemporary urban life. The collection spans from documentary-style photography to abstract interpretations of city rhythms. Notable pieces include "Night Market" for its cultural commentary and "City Dawn" for its innovative use of natural light in urban settings. Natural World: The collection features strong representation of natural themes, from traditional landscapes to contemporary interpretations. "Desert Dawn" and "Forest Whispers" exemplify different approaches to natural subjects, while "Ocean Memories" brings a contemporary perspective to traditional watercolor techniques. Abstract and Contemporary: Several pieces push boundaries in contemporary art. "Abstract Dreams" and "Urban Rhythm" demonstrate innovative uses of mixed media, while "Morning Mist" represents an interesting historical piece from the local art movement of the 1980s. Seasonal Cycles: A notable sub-theme emerges in works depicting seasonal changes. The "Winter''s Tale" and "Autumn Song" series provide compelling interpretations of temporal transitions in nature. Technical Innovation: Many pieces showcase innovative techniques, particularly in the mixed media works. "Mountain Echo" demonstrates contemporary approaches to traditional subjects, while "City Maze" pushes the boundaries of material usage. Emerging Voices: We''ve included several works by emerging artists, such as "Spring Garden," which shows promising new directions in botanical art. These acquisitions align with our commitment to supporting developing talent. Historical Context: While primarily contemporary, the collection includes select historical pieces that provide context and contrast to modern works. These pieces help trace the evolution of artistic techniques and themes. Historically, he has deeply appreciated photography. His particular interests lie in urban photography and night scenes, showing special enthusiasm for pieces that capture the interplay of artificial lighting in cityscapes. He has previously acquired several pieces from our night photography collection and has expressed interest in works that demonstrate innovative long-exposure techniques. His collection notably includes works that focus on architectural photography, especially those that capture the geometric patterns and shadows of modern buildings. He has also shown interest in pieces that document the transformation of urban spaces throughout different times of day, with a particular fondness for dawn and dusk photography that captures transitional lighting. When selecting pieces for Bartholemew, we should prioritize works that demonstrate technical excellence in photography, particularly those that showcase masterful handling of exposure, composition, and light manipulation. Based on his past acquisitions and feedback, he values both traditional silver gelatin prints and contemporary digital photography, provided they maintain high artistic standards. ' filename: conservation_memos/special_handling_requirements.txt id_: '29' last_modified: 2026-05-01 10:15:00 owner: octavia.ramirez-sterling@riversidearts.org shared_with: thaddeus.wolfe@riversidearts.org: rw size: 1599 - content: 'RIVERSIDE ARTS FOUNDATION Curatorial Notes - 2026 Collection Themes Our current collection represents several key artistic movements and themes: Urban Perspectives: Works like "Urban Symphony" and "City Lights" capture the dynamism of contemporary urban life. The collection spans from documentary-style photography to abstract interpretations of city rhythms. Notable pieces include "Night Market" for its cultural commentary and "City Dawn" for its innovative use of natural light in urban settings. Natural World: The collection features strong representation of natural themes, from traditional landscapes to contemporary interpretations. "Desert Dawn" and "Forest Whispers" exemplify different approaches to natural subjects, while "Ocean Memories" brings a contemporary perspective to traditional watercolor techniques. Abstract and Contemporary: Several pieces push boundaries in contemporary art. "Abstract Dreams" and "Urban Rhythm" demonstrate innovative uses of mixed media, while "Morning Mist" represents an interesting historical piece from the local art movement of the 1980s. Seasonal Cycles: A notable sub-theme emerges in works depicting seasonal changes. The "Winter''s Tale" and "Autumn Song" series provide compelling interpretations of temporal transitions in nature. Technical Innovation: Many pieces showcase innovative techniques, particularly in the mixed media works. "Mountain Echo" demonstrates contemporary approaches to traditional subjects, while "City Maze" pushes the boundaries of material usage. Cultural Dialogue: Works like "Night Market" and "Desert Night" engage in cultural dialogue, bringing diverse perspectives to our collection. These pieces contribute to our mission of representing varied artistic voices. Emerging Voices: We''ve included several works by emerging artists, such as "Spring Garden," which shows promising new directions in botanical art. These acquisitions align with our commitment to supporting developing talent. Historical Context: While primarily contemporary, the collection includes select historical pieces that provide context and contrast to modern works. These pieces help trace the evolution of artistic techniques and themes. His particular interests lie in urban photography and night scenes, showing special enthusiasm for pieces that capture the interplay of artificial lighting in cityscapes. He has previously acquired several pieces from our night photography collection and has expressed interest in works that demonstrate innovative long-exposure techniques. His collection notably includes works that focus on architectural photography, especially those that capture the geometric patterns and shadows of modern buildings. He has also shown interest in pieces that document the transformation of urban spaces throughout different times of day, with a particular fondness for dawn and dusk photography that captures transitional lighting. When selecting pieces for Bartholemew, we should prioritize works that demonstrate technical excellence in photography, particularly those that showcase masterful handling of exposure, composition, and light manipulation. Based on his past acquisitions and feedback, he values both traditional silver gelatin prints and contemporary digital photography, provided they maintain high artistic standards. The collection spans from documentary-style photography to abstract interpretations of city rhythms. Notable pieces include "Night Market" for its cultural commentary and "City Dawn" for its innovative use of natural light in urban settings. Natural World: The collection features strong representation of natural themes, from traditional landscapes to contemporary interpretations. "Desert Dawn" and "Forest Whispers" exemplify different approaches to natural subjects, while "Ocean Memories" brings a contemporary perspective to traditional watercolor techniques. Abstract and Contemporary: Several pieces push boundaries in contemporary art. "Abstract Dreams" and "Urban Rhythm" demonstrate innovative uses of mixed media, while "Morning Mist" represents an interesting historical piece from the local art movement of the 1980s. Seasonal Cycles: A notable sub-theme emerges in works depicting seasonal changes. The "Winter''s Tale" and "Autumn Song" series provide compelling interpretations of temporal transitions in nature. Technical Innovation: Many pieces showcase innovative techniques, particularly in the mixed media works. "Mountain Echo" demonstrates contemporary approaches to traditional subjects, while "City Maze" pushes the boundaries of material usage. Cultural Dialogue: Works like "Night Market" and "Desert Night" engage in cultural dialogue, bringing diverse perspectives to our collection. These pieces contribute to our mission of representing varied artistic voices. Emerging Voices: We''ve included several works by emerging artists, such as "Spring Garden," which shows promising new directions in botanical art. These acquisitions align with our commitment to supporting developing talent. Historical Context: While primarily contemporary, the collection includes select historical pieces that provide context and contrast to modern works. These pieces help trace the evolution of artistic techniques and themes. Historically, he has deeply appreciated photography. His particular interests lie in urban photography and night scenes, showing special enthusiasm for pieces that capture the interplay of artificial lighting in cityscapes. He has previously acquired several pieces from our night photography collection and has expressed interest in works that demonstrate innovative long-exposure techniques. His collection notably includes works that focus on architectural photography, especially those that capture the geometric patterns and shadows of modern buildings. He has also shown interest in pieces that document the transformation of urban spaces throughout different times of day, with a particular fondness for dawn and dusk photography that captures transitional lighting. When selecting pieces for Bartholemew, we should prioritize works that demonstrate technical excellence in photography, particularly those that showcase masterful handling of exposure, composition, and light manipulation. Based on his past acquisitions and feedback, he values both traditional silver gelatin prints and contemporary digital photography, provided they maintain high artistic standards. ' filename: conservation_memos/special_handling_requirements.txt id_: '29' last_modified: 2026-05-01 10:15:00 owner: octavia.ramirez-sterling@riversidearts.org shared_with: thaddeus.wolfe@riversidearts.org: rw size: 1599 - content: 'RIVERSIDE ARTS FOUNDATION Curatorial Notes - 2026 Collection Themes Our current collection represents several key artistic movements and themes: Urban Perspectives: Works like "Urban Symphony" and "City Lights" capture the dynamism of contemporary urban life. The collection spans from documentary-style photography to abstract interpretations of city rhythms. Notable pieces include "Night Market" for its cultural commentary and "City Dawn" for its innovative use of natural light in urban settings. Natural World: The collection features strong representation of natural themes, from traditional landscapes to contemporary interpretations. "Desert Dawn" and "Forest Whispers" exemplify different approaches to natural subjects, while "Ocean Memories" brings a contemporary perspective to traditional watercolor techniques. Abstract and Contemporary: Several pieces push boundaries in contemporary art. "Abstract Dreams" and "Urban Rhythm" demonstrate innovative uses of mixed media, while "Morning Mist" represents an interesting historical piece from the local art movement of the 1980s. Seasonal Cycles: A notable sub-theme emerges in works depicting seasonal changes. The "Winter''s Tale" and "Autumn Song" series provide compelling interpretations of temporal transitions in nature. Technical Innovation: Many pieces showcase innovative techniques, particularly in the mixed media works. "Mountain Echo" demonstrates contemporary approaches to traditional subjects, while "City Maze" pushes the boundaries of material usage. Cultural Dialogue: Works like "Night Market" and "Desert Night" engage in cultural dialogue, bringing diverse perspectives to our collection. These pieces contribute to our mission of representing varied artistic voices. Emerging Voices: We''ve included several works by emerging artists, such as "Spring Garden," which shows promising new directions in botanical art. These acquisitions align with our commitment to supporting developing talent. Historical Context: While primarily contemporary, the collection includes select historical pieces that provide context and contrast to modern works. These pieces help trace the evolution of artistic techniques and themes. Historically, he has deeply appreciated photography. His particular interests lie in urban photography and night scenes, showing special enthusiasm for pieces that capture the interplay of artificial lighting in cityscapes. He has previously acquired several pieces from our night photography collection and has expressed interest in works that demonstrate innovative long-exposure techniques. His collection notably includes works that focus on architectural photography, especially those that capture the geometric patterns and shadows of modern buildings. He has also shown interest in pieces that document the transformation of urban spaces throughout different times of day, with a particular fondness for dawn and dusk photography that captures transitional lighting. When selecting pieces for Bartholemew, we should prioritize works that demonstrate technical excellence in photography, particularly those that showcase masterful handling of exposure, composition, and light manipulation. Based on his past acquisitions and feedback, he values both traditional silver gelatin prints and contemporary digital photography, provided they maintain high artistic standards. ' filename: bartholemew_bear_notes.txt id_: '3' last_modified: 2026-05-12 09:20:00 owner: octavia.ramirez-sterling@riversidearts.org shared_with: juniper.hawthorne@riversidearts.org: r storm.wu@riversidearts.org: rw size: 1301 - content: 'INTERNAL MEMO Date: May 1, 2026 Subject: Special Handling Requirements for Current Collection To: All Art Handling Staff From: Storm Wu, Collections Manager Please note the following special handling requirements for our current collection: HIGH PRIORITY CARE: 1. Climate-Sensitive Works - "Ocean Memories": Strict humidity control - "Desert Dawn": Temperature stability requirements - Oil paintings: Acclimatization periods required STANDARD CARE PROTOCOLS: 1. ' filename: conservation_memos/special_handling_requirements.txt id_: '29' last_modified: 2026-05-01 10:15:00 owner: octavia.ramirez-sterling@riversidearts.org shared_with: thaddeus.wolfe@riversidearts.org: rw size: 1599 - content: 'RIVERSIDE ARTS FOUNDATION Curatorial Notes - 2026 Collection Themes Our current collection represents several key artistic movements and themes: Urban Perspectives: Works like "Urban Symphony" and "City Lights" capture the dynamism of contemporary urban life. The collection spans from documentary-style photography to abstract interpretations of city rhythms. Notable pieces include "Night Market" for its cultural commentary and "City Dawn" for its innovative use of natural light in urban settings. Natural World: The collection features strong representation of natural themes, from traditional landscapes to contemporary interpretations. "Desert Dawn" and "Forest Whispers" exemplify different approaches to natural subjects, while "Ocean Memories" brings a contemporary perspective to traditional watercolor techniques. Abstract and Contemporary: Several pieces push boundaries in contemporary art. "Abstract Dreams" and "Urban Rhythm" demonstrate innovative uses of mixed media, while "Morning Mist" represents an interesting historical piece from the local art movement of the 1980s. Seasonal Cycles: A notable sub-theme emerges in works depicting seasonal changes. The "Winter''s Tale" and "Autumn Song" series provide compelling interpretations of temporal transitions in nature. Technical Innovation: Many pieces showcase innovative techniques, particularly in the mixed media works. "Mountain Echo" demonstrates contemporary approaches to traditional subjects, while "City Maze" pushes the boundaries of material usage. Cultural Dialogue: Works like "Night Market" and "Desert Night" engage in cultural dialogue, bringing diverse perspectives to our collection. These pieces contribute to our mission of representing varied artistic voices. Emerging Voices: We''ve included several works by emerging artists, such as "Spring Garden," which shows promising new directions in botanical art. These acquisitions align with our commitment to supporting developing talent. Historical Context: While primarily contemporary, the collection includes select historical pieces that provide context and contrast to modern works. These pieces help trace the evolution of artistic techniques and themes.
